Parked for 49 Years: 1971 Pontiac Needs Restoration, Mixed News Under the Hood
28 photos
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us
Sitting since 1977. This is the first thing you must know about this Trans Am, with the car begging for a complete restoration after spending all these decades away from the road.
Before it can even start dreaming about this long overdue return to the road, the Pontiac has another big mission to accomplish. It must find a home, as the owner posted it on eBay, along with a few specifics about its past.
Most of the original parts are on the car, according to the owner, and that’s the good news. The bad news is that the Trans Am hides a non-original block under the hood, so if you’re here specifically because you want an all-original Pontiac , you’ll just have to look somewhere else.
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us The Trans Am was still in its early days in 1971. Having been launched in 1969, the Trans Am accounted for only 2,116 orders two years later, therefore being the rarest configuration in 1971.
The base Firebird dominated the lineup with 23,021 cars sold to American buyers, followed by the Esprit that accounted for 20,185 units. The Formula was more than three times as popular as the Trans Am, representing 7,802 cars.
1971 was a year when the muscle under the hood still played an important role for American drivers, and despite the push for smaller displacement and more efficient engines, Pontiac didn’t want to give up on big engines.
It reduced the compression but upgraded the 400ci unit on the Trans Am to 455 cubic inches. Known as 455-HO, this engine was the only choice on the Trans Am, though it was offered with either a manual or an automatic transmission. Most people picked the automatic, while the manual made its way to 885 cars.
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us The Trans Am was only offered in two visual configurations. You could get the car either in Cameo White with blue stripes or in Lucerne Blue with white stripes.
This 1971 Trans Am sports the white paint with blue stripes, though it’s unclear if this is the factory spray. I would call the seller and ask for more specifics on this front, but as I said every time I come across a mysterious car, nothing beats a live inspection. Just go there in person to check everything live, as there’s always a good chance that you’ll discover more than what you find online.
Otherwise, this Trans Am hasn’t moved in so many decades, and we all know what this means from a mechanical perspective. While the block isn’t original, it does sport the 1971 casting, so it’s a correct unit that somehow ended up in this Trans Am.
It’s unclear what happened with the original engine, but considering the many years of sitting, I wouldn’t be surprised to discover that the factory unit was seized and the owner found a replacement once they decided to bring the car back to the road.
This Trans Am needs a complete restoration, and the seller also includes a new interior. There are many other parts that you’ll get with this Pontiac, so in many ways, the restoration process has already been jump-started to pave the way for a faster return to the road.
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us The car has over 83,000 miles on it, according to the seller, and considering it’s been sitting for so many years, the original owner enjoyed driving it quite a lot. The Trans Am was parked in 1977, so all these miles were added in only 6 years.
There’s one very important thing you must remember about this Trans Am. It sells without a transmission, so depending on your choice, you can go either for a manual or pick an automatic. A manual would be the right way to enjoy driving this car, but automatics are easier to find, though this also depends on where you live and whether you can find a gearbox fast.
Otherwise, this Trans Am looks doable, and if you don’t mind the non-original setup, it could be a fantastic project that could end up becoming quite a head-turner.
The selling price could be an issue, though. Sure, it’s a 1971 model, and these cars are pretty rare, considering only a few have been made, in the first place. But without the original engine under the hood, it might be hard to convince a restoration guy to pay $46,500 for this car.
The owner also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, so they might be interested in discussing the asking price if you’re committed to a purchase. 30 people added this Trans Am to their watchlists, and considering the listing expires in 28 days, the number could increase significantly in the coming weeks.
Meanwhile, the car is parked in Lemont, Illinois, and given that the engine no longer starts or runs, you will need transportation to take it home. Just make sure it’s large enough to get all the extra parts.

Alternate Future C9 Chevrolet Corvette Still Has an Engine But Also New Space-Age Design Traits
7 photos
Photo: t__mjh /Instagram
It’s been ‘a minute’ since General Motors approved the Corvette project back in 1953, and over the course of eight generations it has grown and even overshadowed its role as ‘America’s quintessential sports car,’ especially after it switched to the C8 iteration.
The Chevrolet Corvette only experienced two major shocks during its lifetime – once when it switched from the inaugural C1 design to the classic style introduced with the C2, and the second time when the established front-engine RWD setup was thrown down the drain for a new mid-engine platform with the introduction of the C8.
After that, innovations and records flowed: the Z06 has the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever made for production models, the 2027 Stingray and Grand Sport have the new 6.7-liter V8 with the most torque of any such NA engine (520 lb-ft of torque, 705 Nm), while the twin-turbo ZR1 and hybrid ZR1X have obviously entered supercar territory with their powerful 1,064-hp and 1,250-hp powertrains.
As such, it’s no wonder that everyone keeps a close eye on the past, present, and future of the Chevrolet Corvette – just recently, a new report from across the rumor mill claims that the Corvette SUV and sedan might not happen, after all, as GM thinks about going against the possibility of diluting the nameplate’s seven decades of sports car legacy.
Also, the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI always seem to have an opinion about the past, present, and future of the Corvette. For example, Tom Hylton, an Exterior and Interior Designer for GAC Milano also moonlights as a virtual artist under the guise of ' t__mjh ' on social media.
Not long ago, his unofficial, hypothetical design project dubbed ‘ Product of Environment – USA ’ featured no less than five different vehicle designs (a fresh Peterbilt truck concept, a three-wheel “City Box,” a Caddy coupe, and a single-seater prototype) and also included the grand finale of an alternate timeline Chevrolet Corvette that’s contemporary with us but looked both retro and futuristic at the same time and kept the V8 firmly planted under the front hood.
Now he again muses about a potential Chevy Corvette, maybe the upcoming C9 iteration, and this time around it’s a mid-engine version as far as we can tell. It’s appropriate for the New Space Age in terms of design, with minimalistic lines and a low cabin that still includes two big-sized leather-wrapped bucket seats.
The wedge shape reminds us of Lamborghini, but it won’t be accused of copying any of the Italian supercars due to the quirky rear, which includes a tiny vertical rear window to go along with the pointy back design, the slim LED taillights, plus the singular oval exhaust outlet. So, this project is either ICE or HEV, not all-electric, for sure. Cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Tom (@t__mjh)

Mansory Rolls-Royce Phantom Looks Like It Demands Your First Born Just To Open the Door
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | mansory.usa
Is there such a thing as too many tuned Rolls-Royce Phantoms ? Well, it depends on whom you ask, because while purists would argue that the massive luxury sedan is best had with zero modifications, some petrolheads would definitely say that the car world needs more tuned examples of this luxury land yacht.
Therefore, a small albeit high-end chunk of the tuning world has plenty of upgrades on its shelves for the British brand’s model that roams on its own, with no direct rivals in sight. That’s because the Phantom is much larger and a lot more expensive than the Bentley Flying Spur and the Mercedes-Maybach S-Class, as these are direct competitors to the Rolls-Royce Ghost, in case you forgot, and some say that the Ghost absolutely dominates its class, whereas others would get a Maybach or a Flying Spur all day, any day.
Guess it’s a matter of personal taste, and for what it’s worth, I’d always get a Ghost over its direct rivals, even if the one I drove a few years back was on the squeaky side of things. And I’d also get a Phantom for a chauffeured experience, as there is really nothing like this dinosaur in today’s car game, is there? Now, as for the tuning part, several companies offer all kinds of “upgrades” for the Rolls-Royce Phantom, from various exterior add-ons and new wheels, to custom interiors and more oomph.
Mansory’s name is at the very top of the list, because this tuner has signed numerous Rolls-Royce Phantoms over the years. Some were quite hideous, others were nice, and this example, which came directly from the company’s US branch on social media, with the pictures shared earlier in the week, is not bad at all to be honest. Sure, it’s also not great, but for a Mansory, it is actually a head-turner for all the right reasons, isn’t it?
Photo: Instagram | mansory.usa The makeover is quite familiar, as we have seen it on other Rolls-Royce Phantoms from Mansory. It includes a reworked section of the lower bumper, with a redesigned air intake, additional daytime running light strips on the sides, and an apron with side blades on the lower part. The main grille has been tweaked color-wise, and so has the Spirit of Ecstasy hood emblem that disappears at the touch of a screen (or if you want to steal it).
Further back, we can see that the trim on the front fenders has been tweaked, and that there are some side skirt attachments as well, which are part of the makeover. The ducktail spoiler, the piece added at the bottom of the rear windscreen, and the diffuser are also new, and they are not flashy at all, are they? The wheels have also come from Mansory’s portfolio, and they have a satin black look, just like the rest of the car, which sits closer to the ground, and the orange accents, including the pinstripe, contrast the exterior.
Mind you, those orange touches are not there for nothing, because the tie the exterior of this modified Rolls-Royce Phantom to the cockpit. Here, the orange leather upholstery can be seen on the seats, door cards, parts of the dashboard panel, center console, and even on the roof, as well as on other touchable elements. There is also some black leather upholstery on deck for a bit of contrast, black piping, and the black RR logo embroidered into the headrests.
Photo: Instagram | mansory.usa There is no real way of telling whether the cabin of this particular Rolls-Royce Phantom was the work of Mansory, of it the luxury land yacht has come like this from the Goodwood factory, where this generation of the model has come to life ever since 2017, as the automaker offers numerous personalization items for its flagship sedan. And yes, lively colors are also on the list, alongside a plethora of other shades.
According to the tuner, the vehicle in question is said to have 610 horsepower. This means that the engine has been tweaked, because it is normally good for 563 horsepower. That’s 571 horsepower for the metric crowd, and 420 kilowatts. The mill is a V12 with twin turbos and a 6.75-liter displacement, which churns out 664 pound-feet (900 Nm) of torque as standard. The Rolls-Royce Phantom takes just over 5 seconds to reach 62 mph (100 kph) from zero, and tops out at 155 mph (250 kph). The EWB is a bit slower.
Now, Mansory hasn’t revealed any other details about this Rolls-Royce Phantom, so it is likely not for sale. But if it were, then this thing would have probably cost close to the seven-digit territory. After all, such projects tend to change hands for huge amounts of money. Do you dig the makeover in this case, with the modified exterior, lowered ground clearance, new wheels, and lively-looking cockpit? Borderlands Mexico is a weekly rundown of developments in the world of United States-Mexico cross-border trucking and trade. This week in Borderlands Mexico: Texas cross-border traffic rises by 400 trucks through Saturday pilot; Truck freight between US and Mexico reaches $75.4B in September; and Teleflex invests $5M in new medical device manufacturing facility in Mexico.
Texas cross-border traffic rises through Saturday pilot program
U.S. Customs and Border Protection expects to extend a pilot program expanding Saturday commercial truck operations at the World Trade Bridge in Laredo, Texas, for another 90 days as officials evaluate changes in cross-border freight traffic.
The pilot, which began Sept. 5, extends Saturday commercial processing by three hours, with operations running from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. The expansion was requested by Mexico’s National Customs Agency (ANAM) and trade stakeholders seeking to improve import and export truck flows .
Armando Taboada Jr., assistant director of field operations for CBP’s Laredo Field Office, said the expanded schedule has been accompanied by increased Saturday truck traffic and declining Sunday volumes.
Taboada said Saturday commercial truck traffic has increased by approximately 400 to 500 trucks, while Sunday crossings are averaging about 300 to 400 fewer trucks.
“It appears that some importers/carriers are shifting some truck crossings from Sundays to Saturdays,” Taboada told FreightWaves.
The shift suggests some cross-border trucking companies and importers are taking advantage of the expanded Saturday operating schedule rather than increasing their overall weekend freight movements.
The initial 90-day pilot is scheduled to conclude in early December, but CBP expects the program to continue for another three months to gather additional data on commercial cargo processing.
“It will depend on the final pilot numbers and input from the City of Laredo, Trade Stakeholders, and CBP,” Taboada said. “The pilot is expected to be extended another 90 days to get a proper gauge of commercial cargo truck processing results.”
Despite the increase in Saturday crossings, CBP has not observed significant congestion or processing delays at the World Trade Bridge.
“For the most part, traffic is steady and no major wait times or processing delays are being experienced,” Taboada said.
He credited improvements in the bridge’s commercial vehicle inspection infrastructure with helping CBP accommodate truck traffic.
Through the City of Laredo’s Donations Acceptance Program contributions, the World Trade Bridge expanded from seven primary inspection lanes to 19, including 15 regular lanes and four Free and Secure Trade (FAST)/Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) lanes.
Taboada said the additional inspection capacity has improved commercial truck processing during weekdays and weekends.
However, weekend commercial traffic remains substantially lower than weekday volumes.
CBP also released preliminary commercial truck and rail crossing statistics covering Aug. 23 through Nov. 7 across the eight ports of entry administered by its Laredo Field Office.
The figures include commercial truck movements at the World Trade Bridge, Colombia-Solidarity Bridge, Eagle Pass, Brownsville, Pharr, Hidalgo and other South Texas crossings.
The report also includes rail activity at Laredo, Eagle Pass and Brownsville, offering a broader view of commercial freight movements between Mexico and the United States.
The World Trade Bridge continues to account for a substantial share of commercial truck traffic in the Laredo Field Office, underscoring the importance of the crossing to U.S.-Mexico trade.
Truck freight between US and Mexico reaches $75.4B in September
The value of goods transported by trucks between the U.S. and Mexico reached $75.4 billion in September, accounting for approximately 78% of the $96.3 billion in total trade between the two countries, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS).
Total U.S.-Mexico freight trade increased 34.2% compared with September 2025, according to a BTS report released Friday.
Across both the U.S.-Mexico and U.S.-Canada borders, trucks transported $109.7 billion in freight during September, a 27.6% increase compared with the same month last year.
Combined North American transborder freight totaled $161.1 billion, up 23.4% year over year. U.S.-Canada freight accounted for $64.8 billion, a 10.1% increase.
Rail shipments between the United States and Mexico totaled $8.3 billion in September, followed by vessel freight at $6.5 billion, air cargo at $2.8 billion and pipeline shipments at $900 million.
Laredo, Texas, remained the leading U.S. truck freight gateway, with $38.1 billion in total cross-border freight across transportation modes during September, according to BTS. El Paso, Texas, and Otay Mesa, California, were also among the leading truck crossings for U.S.-Mexico trade.
The figures underscore trucking’s dominant role in North American trade, particularly along the U.S.-Mexico border, where manufacturers and shippers rely heavily on commercial vehicles to move goods between the two countries.
Teleflex invests $5M in new medical device manufacturing facility in Mexico
U.S.-based medical technology manufacturer Teleflex has inaugurated a $5 million machining facility in Chihuahua, Mexico, expanding its manufacturing capabilities for medical devices and specialized components.
The new 8,073-square-foot facility will manufacture high-precision tooling and components used in medical device production, according to a report by Mexico Industry .
The investment strengthens Teleflex’s existing manufacturing operations in Chihuahua, where the company operates four production plants employing approximately 2,000 workers.
The new machining workshop is designed to expand the company’s ability to produce specialized tools and precision components required for medical equipment manufacturing.
Headquartered in Wayne, Pennsylvania, Teleflex develops and manufactures medical technologies used in vascular access, interventional cardiology, anesthesia, surgery, urology and emergency medicine. The company serves U.S. healthcare providers and hospitals.
Teleflex operates in 36 countries and serves health care providers in more than 150 markets.
Why it matters: U.S. Customs and Border Protection officials say extended weekend hours could provide more scheduling flexibility for cross-border carriers and shippers without significantly increasing processing delays.

Unapologetic Mercedes-Benz GT Design Project Was Done by an Intern; It's Ready for Cannonball 2030
12 photos
Photo: cardesignworld / Instagram
Just recently, Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kallenius confirmed at the Golden Steering Wheel awards in Berlin that his company will introduce a new SL version for 2027, separating the series into three distinct personalities.
There’s the initial AMG version as well as the ultra-luxurious Maybach, and soon there will be a comfort-focused model which probably reverts the nameplate to a Mercedes-Benz moniker. The company also has another type of vehicle at the top of the ‘sports car’ category – the all-new second-generation Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupé (C590), aka the sports brand’s first dedicated all-electric performance model.
It rides on the bespoke 800-volt AMG.EA architecture and was revealed earlier in 2026 with YASA-developed axial-flux electric motors and F1-derived battery technology, plus up to 1,169 hp for the top GT 63 4Matic+ model. It was swiftly followed by the GT SUV sibling, and both have been at the center of intense discussions about Mercedes’ new EV styling, which has been pretty controversial, to say the least.
But there are other ways to be unapologetic in terms of design and still make a positive impact on Mercedes-Benz fans: the good folks over at Car Design World (aka ' cardesignworld ' on social media) tipped us off to this official intern design project by artist Lukas Worsche, who recently completed a Mercedes Advanced Design Internship and wrapped up the stage with his own take on a Mercedes GT sports car.
The idea was pretty wacky, indeed: What if Mercedes developed a car specifically for the Cannonball Run? By the way, the Cannonball Run is a 1981 action-comedy film starring an all-star ensemble cast, including Burt Reynolds, Dom DeLuise, Roger Moore, Farrah Fawcett, Jackie Chan, Sammy Davis Jr., and Dean Martin, inspired by an actual cross-country outlaw road race – the 1979 running of the Cannonball Baker Sea-to-Shining-Sea Memorial Trophy Dash.
Today, the modern Cannonball Run is an unsanctioned speed record attempt that involves driving across the US, traditionally from New York City's Red Ball Garage to the Portofino Hotel in Redondo Beach, California, near Los Angeles, running a distance of about 2,813 miles (4,527 km). The current record was achieved in May 2020 during early Covid-19 lockdowns, but that doesn’t mean it was any less perilous because of the sustained high speeds.
Anyway, this Mercedes GT would be a purpose-built machine for the Cannonball Run, but other than that, its unapologetic design works extremely well for an alternate option to the GT 4-Door EV, as this coupe has the allure of a traditional grand tourer but also the muscle of an EV supercar. There are massive aerodynamic elements, muscly fenders, a small cabin, and a huge front hood, along with an extreme powertrain.
As far as we can tell, the artist chose ‘direction 2’ of the project, which apparently involves a hybrid powertrain using separate wheel hub electric motors at the rear along with two compact jet turbines for the front, one each in the oversized front fenders! 2028 Lexus RX Mid-Cycle Refresh Debuts Virtually, Featuring Both Styling and Technical Updates
22 photos
Photo: TopElectricSUV.com
The premium Japanese automaker Lexus has been pretty busy with its collection of 2027 model year changes and updates: they put a price tag on the 2027 RZ in the States, gave the 2027 NX multiple upgrades and a touch of Mars, and the family-oriented TX bid farewell to the slow-selling and expensive 550h+ plug-in hybrid, leaving the rest of the range to get the latest upgrades.
How about the most popular Lexus RX ? Well, following the facelift of the second-gen NX, Lexus is reportedly working around the clock on the next big thing – the mid-cycle refresh for the fifth-gen RX, which has been around since the spring of 2022 and is being tested for its facelift, as per our spy photographer partners.
Well, the rumor mill also wants to contribute, and the good folks from the " TopElectricSUV " news outlet have some thoughts about the BMW X5 Neue Klasse rival, along with illustrations thanks to their member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to aid their cause.
In terms of design, Lexus is not expected to implement major changes – just cosmetic revisions like restyled headlamp graphics and a fresh bumper at the front along with a reworked ‘spindle body’ grille. New alloy wheels might also arrive, and there’s also a potential refresh of the rear with new taillight graphics and minor adjustments to the bumper.
On the other hand, bigger changes might arrive inside, where Lexus is rumored to switch to a slimmer and less cluttered dashboard for a cleaner look – it could follow the guidelines of the all-new ES with a separate 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and a free-standing 14-inch infotainment screen.
It could still have touch-operated climate controls, but the software and processing power could be newer and more efficient. Last but not least, a new steering wheel might also arrive. Currently, Lexus offers three powertrains for the RX, all electrified: 246 hp hybrid (RX 350h), the 366-hp for the 500h, and 304 hp for the 450h+ plug-in hybrid.
However, the facelift might bring the sixth-generation Lexus hybrid technology for both HEV and PHEV applications, with improved fuel efficiency thanks to the use of silicon-carbide (SiC) semiconductors and lower overall weight.
The plug-in hybrid model could see larger changes – a bigger 22.7 kWh battery pack for additional EV range along with a slight power bump that could match the 324 combined hp offered by the latest RAV4 PHEV. Charging could also become faster with support for 50 kW DC at fast-charging stations. So, what do you think about these proposed changes? Will they make the RX a worthier opponent for the likes of the Volvo XC60, the Neue Klasse BMW X5, and the recently facelifted Mercedes GLE?

The 2027 Bullet Crossfire 245RKS Is Half-Ton Towable, Value-Oriented, and Oh So Nice
20 photos
Photo: YouTube/Field and Sports Report
Just because something is described as value-oriented or budget-friendly doesn't mean that it's cheap in the worst sense of the word. The Bullet Crossfire travel trailer from Keystone RV is the perfect example of that in the RV segment.
Keystone's Bullet series of travel trailers was launched as just that: value-oriented products that ticked several boxes, including towability, comfort, and even extended autonomy. Over the years, Keystone further refined the series, dividing it into three layers depending on the degree of comfort and spec they offered.
The Bullet Crossfire is the mid-tier Bullet, itself divided into several floorplans. The Bullet Crossfire 245RKS is one of the most popular in the series, a rear kitchen floorplan that offers sleeping for as many as six people, and all the creature comforts of home. The best part is that it does all this without breaking the bank.
For the 2027 model year, Keystone is further upgrading and refining the Bullet, introducing for the Crossfire sub-series a new exterior, an upgraded interior with new cabinetry and hardware, and better tech.
Photo: YouTube/Field and Sports Report As you can see in the overly enthusiastic video tour at the bottom of the page, this allows the 2027 Bullet Crossfire 245RKS to go from a value-oriented travel trailer to a nice family option that might even be capable of some mild boondocking.
Construction is the same as with the other Bullets, and that means no wood, all-composite shell with HyperCore sidewalls under a layer of fiberglass, HyperDeck composite flooring, a fully walkable roof, and a redesigned molded fiberglass front cap that will definitely get some eyeballs at camp. Getting attention must be last on the list of priorities when buying a new RV, but nice aesthetics do matter.
The Bullet Crossfire 245RKS comes in at 28.8 feet (8.7 meters) of total length and rides on a tandem axle equipped with Lippert Road Armor suspension and Goodyear tires.
Photo: YouTube/Field and Sports Report Standard spec includes a power tongue jack with a hardcover box for a pair of propane tanks, power stabilizer jacks, solid composite entry steps with adjustable legs, and Solar Flex standard that gets you a 220W of solar on the roof (upgradable to 660W), a 30-amp Victron controller, prep for a 2000W inverter, and seven inverted outlets onboard.
This floorplan is a two-door, single-slide one, which makes it perfect for traveling families as it offers the right amount of space and privacy to co-exist even for longer stretches. To that same end, it uses a pass-through mid bathroom, while making room onboard for a dedicated dining space and storage for all six people.
One entrances is directly into the front bedroom, while the other gives into the rear kitchen and open-plan living room. A large 12V fridge with freezer and Thomas Payne theater seats that you can swap out for a tri-fold sofa to get that six-person sleeping capacity occupy the single slide-out, which is flush-floor for maximum comfort.
Photo: YouTube/Field and Sports Report The rear kitchen takes up the entire width at the back, so it's a single-block one. Still, it's nicely appointed and spacious enough to allow even two cooks working side by side, with a three-burner gas cooktop, an RV-size oven, a Furrion extractor, and a Furrion microwave with air fryer function.
Keystone boasts the tallest height in its class for the Bullet, which means 82 inches (208 cm) f headroom, which, in turn, means you get extra storage in overhead cabinets. For good measure, the kitchen also offers under-the-counter storage, but you have the possibility to extend kitchen storage in the dinette or overhead in the slide.
Cabinets come with strong magnetic latches and either latticed or glass-like faces, which saves weight and money without feeling as if it's a compromise.
Photo: YouTube/Field and Sports Report The booth-style dinette converts into a third bed and offers a 32-inch 12V TV on a swivel overhead, perfectly positioned for viewing from the theater seats in the slide-out. Also here, you get a pantry and a full wardrobe across the way, with an electric fireplace added for the atmosphere and as an extra heat source.
The bathroom is a standard pass-through one, but finished with the same residential touches , proving that, indeed, it's the little things that make a difference. You get a shower with a full fiberglass surround, an extra-high skylight, and a squeegee door, a porcelain foot-flush toilet, and a sink on a vanity that actually offers ample storage wherever possible.
Two barn doors on either side of the bathroom allow for much-needed privacy. You can close off the main bedroom and create some separation between those sleeping here and the four guests in the front part of the trailer.
Photo: YouTube/Field and Sports Report Speaking of the bedroom, it comes with a true queen bed on an aluminum-slatted base with extra storage and gas struts for each access, overhead cabinets, matching wardrobes, and accent lights.
The Bullet Crossfire 245RKS comes with a best-in-class 18,000-BTU Furrion Chill Cube AC in the living room space, a second 8,000-BTU unit in the bedroom, ducted furnace, an on-demand water heater, and oversize holding tanks. That means 54 gallons (204 liters) of freshwater, 76 gallons (287 liters) of gray, and 38 gallons (144 liters) of black water.
Another advantage of this floorplan is the fact that it's manageable in size and half-ton towable. Empty weight is listed at 6,115 lbs (2,774 kg), with 7,600 lbs (3,447 kg) of gross weight.
Photo: YouTube/Field and Sports Report The 2027 Keystone Bullet Crossfire 245RKS is selling for prices ranging $34,000-$42,000, depending on options and the dealer you get your unit from. It's not "cheap," but it is good value for everything it offers .

Lucid’s Cosmos Sub-$50K EV Imagined, Do You Like the Design?
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
Lucid Motors has three main models in its current lineup . These are called the Air, Gravity, and Sapphire, and EV enthusiasts (and not only) know everything there is to know about them.
Is there room for improvement in the company’s current portfolio? The answer to this question is obviously yes, and the automaker is doing just that. You likely know that Lucid has a more affordable electric vehicle in the making, because it was supposed to hit the assembly line at the end of the year (2026). However, it was eventually delayed, and now interested parties will have to wait until the second half of 2027 to get their hands on it.
The model is called the Lucid Cosmos , and it will be the auto marque’s first vehicle fully built at their plant. In case you forgot, it is a crossover that will take on the likes of the Tesla Model Y and Rivian R2, and will be priced at under $50,000. The entry-level grade is expected to kick off in the high $40,000s, though opting for a better-equipped model, supposedly with more oomph available on tap, might require paying over $70,000.
Lucid’s Cosmos is understood to be based on a new platform, which will also be the foundation stone of the Earth, because the Cosmos is not the only model in the pipeline. Further more, a third vehicle, whose name is yet unknown, will be based on this construction as well. New motors are understood to be on deck, though details surrounding the output and thrust are unknown at this point, and will be released in due course.
Photo: Kolesa Now, while we may not know much about the Lucid Cosmos , we do know what it will look like. That’s because a set of patent images surfaced a few months ago, revealing the styling of the upcoming model from a few angles. And guess what? These drawings served as a foundation stone for the digital illustrations signed by Nikita Chuyko, which were shared online by Kolesa recently.
The model features a tiny grille between the slim LED headlights. The Lucid name is visible above, and further down, we can see a quite large air intake in the middle of the bumper, flanked by the vertical vents. The front fascia looks similar to the one of the larger Gravity, for what it’s worth, and to be honest, we wouldn’t be surprised if this thing featured a light bar at the front, though it is not present in the renderings shared in the gallery.
Further up, we can see a rather small front hood with angular curves on it. The profile looks quite soft for the most part, and this applies to the design of the doors and the roofline. The Lucid Cosmos features flush door handles, and has some angular styling on the lower parts of the doors. Further back, the model features a split-style rear windscreen, a floating-like design for the rear pillars, and a sporty wing stretching across the rear windscreen.
The tailgate is decorated with the backlit Lucid logo, which sits between the ultra thin taillights. The rear bumper also features a quite angular design. We can also see the horizontal reflectors on the lower outer edges, as well as a diffuser-like element. The license plate recess is visible on the bumper. There is way of knowing whether the Lucid lettering will be backlit, or if there will be a light bar stretching across the width of the tailgate as hinted in the patent drawings.
Photo: Kolesa Do you know how most patent images focus solely on the exterior of an upcoming car ? Well, these ones also offered an important glimpse inside. The dashboard panel seems to be dominated by a large screen, and it is yet unknown whether this thing will be split in half, or if there will be three displays, including perhaps one for the front passenger.
The center console has a pair of dials on it, as well as storage further back, and we can also see a pair of air vents for the backseat occupants, and a small cubby above them. Chances are that higher grades will feature rear-seat HVAC controls, too.
Overall, we can say that the upcoming Lucid Cosmos will borrow a few things from the larger Gravity, but it will also carve its own path at the same time, and only time will tell if it is a winning recipe or not. God knows that Lucid deserves a break, because it is struggling. The company is said to have delivered less than 4,000 vehicles in the second quarter of the year, so it likely hopes that the Cosmos might boost their sales overall.
If you were into mid-sized EVs and you saw the Lucid Cosmos looking like it does in these otherwise realistic (for the most part) renderings , would you spend your money on it?

EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Here's How Much a 2025 Rolls-Royce Spectre With 3,000+ Miles Costs in the US
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | mph
Rolls-Royce’s first-ever production electric model, the Spectre , is one of the best luxury grand tourers in its class. Not that there are many left, by the way, yet due to its all-quiet nature, size, and price tag, it does not really have a direct competitor.
It may not show its age yet, though it is already three years old. Deliveries started in the last quarter of 2023, and production takes place at the Goodwood factory in West Sussex, UK. The full-size luxury car could easily transition to an ICE unit, if the company really wanted it, because it is based on the Architecture of Luxury. And this means that it shares numerous nuts and bolts with the Phantom land yacht, the Ghost luxury sedan, and the Cullinan SUV.
Could it eventually gain a gasoline burner? Well, the only one suitable for it would be the hand-built V12, with its twin turbocharged nature, which has a 6.75-liter displacement. And this mill is found on Ghost, Phantom, and Cullinan, in case you forgot. However, while that would be a great addition, this writer believes, it won’t happen, because nothing suggests that Rolls-Royce has something like this in the pipeline for the Spectre .
The model is truly gargantuan for a two-door coupe, as it measures 214.7 inches (5,453 mm) from bumper to bumper. It is 81.9 inches (2,080 mm) wide, 61.4 inches (1,559 mm) tall, and has a wheelbase length of 126.4 inches (3,210 mm). It has a curb weight of almost three metric tons, which is roughly 6,500 pounds, and a future-proof design to die for, both inside and out.
Photo: Instagram | mph If you want to park one of these in your garage, then you must be loaded . That’s because the base model starts from roughly $400,000 in the United States of America for the 2027 model year, whereas the Black Badge variant is around $70,000 more expensive. A nicely-specced example can end up costing you well over half a million dollars, especially if you want the superior Black Badge, which not only gets more goodies, but also offers more oomph.
A used Rolls-Royce Spectre is still on the very expensive side of things, as these tend to fetch from $320,000 to over $500,000 in today’s used car market on our shores, and the value depends on the specification, mileage, and overall condition. Pictured in the gallery is a 2025 model year that features a Black Diamond exterior. It rides on black multi-spoke alloys, has black brake calipers, and is only a few mods away from going down the murdered-out route.
On the inside, this machine features a Muscari Blue look, the vendor reveals. The blue leather upholstery was wrapped around the seats, door cards, center console, and other elements. The lower parts of the dashboard are presented in white, and there is also some black leather upholstery on deck, as well as white piping and stitching. The headliner is black, there are Rolls-Royce emblems embroidered into the headrests, and this thing does not seem to have been visited by the tuning fairy from what we can see.
Photo: Instagram | mph According to the selling dealer, which goes by the name of @mph on Instagram, this particular Rolls-Royce Spectre has a single owner in the papers, and only 3,075 miles (4,949 km) on the clock. Its dual motor setup produces 567 hp (423 kW/575 ps) and 664 pound-feet (900 Nm) of torque. This enables 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in 4.5 seconds. The Black Badge completes the sprint in 4.2 seconds, and has 650 hp (485 kW/659 ps) and 793 lb-ft (1,075 Nm) of torque available via the right pedal.
The vendor mentions a few things about it, including the handcrafted interior, advanced suspension and chassis tech, the magic carpet ride, all-wheel drive, Spirit of Ecstasy hood ornament, and so on, and says that this machine is in stock and ready to be shipped to your doorstep. It appears to be a flawless example, from what we can tell by looking at the pictures shared in the gallery, though for what it’s worth, the driver’s seat appears to show a tiny bit of wear already.
But how much do you think one must fork out if they dream about writing their name on the dotted line of this machine? Well, the pictured Rolls-Royce Spectre, which is a 2025 model year as mentioned above, with just under 3,100 miles under its belt, can be yours today in return for $399,950. And that does not make it affordable, though you may agree to disagree if your bank account has enough digits in it.
Now, if you want to buy this Rolls-Royce Spectre , then you should get in touch with the vendor on social media in order to discuss the details. But would you actually blow $400K on an EV , albeit an extremely luxurious one? View this post on Instagram A post shared by MPH (@mph)

EICMA 2026 • Triumph TF-E Bikes Get Even More Enduro With Updates for the 2027 Model Year
This Dodge Challenger SRT Demon Was Left To Rot, Someone Paid $60,000 for It, but Will It Run?
24 photos
Photo: Percepcar USA | YouTube
There are only 3,300 such cars in the world, and it's hard to believe that someone left one of them abandoned for years, sitting on four flat tires and collecting dust instead of drag strip miles. A car enthusiast specializing in returning run-down, beat-up vehicles to their former glory bought it at auction and is now trying to revive it.
Vagner Moleiro of Percepcar USA bought the car at an auction in Michigan for $60,000. It came without the factory-sealed crate, which takes the power to 840 horsepower. He had no idea if it ran or drove, but he knew that the battery was drained and the pump that cooled the supercharger wasn't working, either. The supercharger, though, came with a big question mark. If it was dead, too, it would cost them $9,500 to replace it.
The listing warned the buyer about all the issues it had. Furthermore, it said: "Do not move the car in the cold on these tires." The car left the auction yard, towed onto the trailer on four flat tires. It was then that Vagner’s lead mechanic, Benjamin, saw a paper with a message left on the only seat on board. The message warned drivers that the tires the car came with were not for rain or for the highway.
"Do not move or drive the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon when temperatures drop below 15 degrees Fahrenheit ( minus 9 degrees Celsius) with the factory Nitto tires installed," is the exact warning about the temperature limit, explicitly outlined in both the 2018 Dodge Challenger Demon Owner's Manual Supplement and the mandatory customer waiver that has to be signed at purchase.
Photo: Percepcar USA | YouTube With all four tires flat and the engine refusing to crank, there was no way the car could move on its own power. The repairs didn’t even kick off before the new owner removed years of mold and dirt, along with the dust that this car had collected instead of miles, over the past few years. So, it was loaded onto the trailer and taken to the shop.
Dust, mold and a missing sealed crate The next morning, the new owner of the long-abandoned Dodge Challenger SRT Demon could see the extent of the damage. The muscle car was covered in a layer of dust and grime, hiding the Plum Crazy paint that once made all heads turn.
The first owner of the Challenger SRT Demon sold the sealed crate separately from the car, so Vagner had to track it down. He found it with a Dodge parts collector. It was still sealed, just the way it left the factory in Ontario. So they paid $4,500 to get the box.
Photo: Percepcar USA | YouTube The Demon Crate is a serialized, factory-optional track kit that the automaker originally sold for $1 with the 2018 Challenger SRT Demo n. It contains specialized performance parts and custom Snap-on tools that the owner would need in order to convert the car from street trim to full drag-strip specification.
Collectors prize unopened, factory-sealed crates just like this one, because each box features an engraved metal plaque matching the specific car's VIN, serial number, and original buyer's name, along with parts that unlock the full 840-horsepower potential on 100+ octane race fuel, which is up from 808 horsepower on pump gas.
The box includes the high-octane PCM module, the replacement switch module, the narrow front skinny aluminum drag wheels measuring 18x4.5 inches, the conical performance air filter, and the passenger mirror block-off plate, which covers the door mount if the passenger-side mirror is removed for racing.
The Challenger SRT Demon finally hits the drag strip Dodge produced 3,300 retail units of the 2018 Challenger SRT Demon for a single model year. All cars were built at the Brampton Assembly Plant in Ontario, Canada. The final car rolled off the production line on May 30, 2018. Production of the Demon resumed in 2023 with a farewell car: the Challenger SRT Demon 170 with its mind-blowing 1,025 horsepower (1,039 metric horsepower).
Photo: Percepcar USA | YouTube Vagner and Benjamin would be happy to hear the 840 horsepower roar from under the hood. A new battery, which is a $1,200 deal, and fresh 100+ octane fuel and coolant do the trick, and the HEMI roared back to life after years of sitting in an abandoned car.
When the temperatures allowed, according to the cold-weather warning left on the seat when they took the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon from the auction yard, they took it straight to an empty drag strip to see how it behaved.
And it checked all the right boxes. The Nittos gripped, the front axle lifted off the ground, and the Demon took off, launching like a rocket, looking like it had been longing for the pavement. This is what Vagner and Benjamin got for the $60,000 they paid at the auction and the nearly $6,000 that they paid for the crate box and the battery.
A 2018 Dodge Challenger SRT Demo n typically sells for around $90,000 to $120,000 in the used car market, depending heavily on mileage, condition, and whether the original Demon Crate is included. Unmodified, delivery-mile examples with under 100 miles, with all factory plastic and an unopened Demon Crate, still command asking prices up to $150,000 to $190,000.
So it looks like what they got is a steal. And this car is no longer going to stay parked, because Benjamin will make sure it was worth every single cent.
